event: Day 34, sixteen days out: Wren feels the dawn vibration tight at its edges.
Palms on the limestone, she finds a deep compression: the substrate gathering tension.
Two days. She journals: dawn vibration full but compressed, substrate tension.
Brecca repoints the gathering hall's north face on her third circuit of the building.
Theron clears the buried southern extension of the drainage channel with his trowel.
Hadley sorts supplies, reckoning food against distance.
Maret sits at the fire pit with her counting rod, listening, unmoved since dawn.
At midday Wren finds her. 'You feel it,' Maret says. 'The substrate is tightening.'
Maret's grandmother said the ground changes two days before the holding.
Through the bond Wren feels the limestone bracing, the way ghost-elms brace before a pulse.
At Known depth she feels the precursor earlier than at Familiar, by hours.
Maret says the builders heard the stone's greeting change four days out.
They had listened for generations; Wren has listened for five weeks.
Day 35: the dawn vibration lasts eighteen seconds, not thirty.
The precursor crowds the stone's frequency, running up from the southwest.
The carried stone at the threshold stone's base is warmer, answering with presence.
She journals: 18 seconds, precursor in the substrate, carried stone responding.
In the afternoon Wren goes to the gap alone; she turns Maret down.
The precursor deepens the suppression field; she won't test it on someone unbonded.
At the gap the dead tree conducts the precursor as a steady pulse into her bones.
She measures the gap: seven degrees, unchanged since Day 29, twenty-six days stable.
Walking back, the compression eases and the threshold stone's warmth returns.
The evening fire is quiet; Hadley narrates less, Brecca's hands grip each other.
Theron sits against the hall wall, watching the tree line.
Maret tells of a three-day storm when she was twelve that scattered her grandmother's herbs.
Her grandmother knelt in the rain picking rosemary: 'You again. Fine. I'm keeping the rosemary.'
Wren's hand goes to the rosemary her mother tucked in her jacket.
Maret sees it: 'Everyone carries something. My grandmother carried rosemary too.'
The insect chorus thins and the ghost-elm hum tightens. One day.
Day 36: Wren is at the threshold stone before light.
Maret comes in the dark with her counting rod and stands at the east face, not touching.
Theron rests his hand in the carved depression on the stone's western side.
Brecca puts both hands flat on the retaining wall: the mason's position.
Hadley stands behind them all with his journal; nobody asked anyone to come.
The dawn vibration does not come; the precursor swallows the greeting.
'It cannot sing,' Maret says. 'The greeting goes quiet. Then the stone remembers.'
At midday the pulse arrives as a directional wave pushing north through the basin.
The insect chorus stops, the ghost-elms stop humming, the substrate vibrates.
The [Foundation Stone] signature expands at once and meets the wave at the margin, and holds.
The triad sings: Enduring, Tended, Kept turn the corruption into information.
Wren holds without clinging: the bond at Known depth holds her in recognition.
Two complete things touch at the bond; the Holding finds nothing incomplete to close on.
The pulse runs past an hour; she loses count.
The carried stone sings with a human warmth, four generations of held intention.
Maret counts the holding on her rod, thumb moving notch to notch.
Brecca holds the wall with full attention: not a bond, not a class, listening.
Theron has gone to the gap's edge to watch and count the second pulse.
The pulse ebbs north; the signature contracts and the triad quiets.
The carried stone's warmth lingers.
A discovery logs the triad's second-pulse signal discrimination: +52 XP, 1941 / 2573.

changes.note: Discovery: Varethen triad network, second pulse

event: She does not calculate the gap to Level 6; she sits at the stone and breathes.
Theron returns from the gap at mid-afternoon: 'Six degrees.'
The southwestern boundary moved one degree: the corruption has never retreated before.
'Twice the gap has held. And this time it moved.' 'Something changed.'
Theron looks at the carried stone: 'My aunt's stone.' 'Your great-great-grandmother's.'
'One degree. That is not nothing.' 'No. That is not nothing.'
At the fire Maret reports the holding: one hundred and twelve slow breaths.
It ran about a fifth longer than the first pulse; Wren reckons nine more minutes.
Maret touched the carried stone during the holding; it was warm, then warmer.
'I have held it ten thousand times. It never felt like that. The stone remembered.'
The System has no word for what Maret felt through her palm.
Hadley hears three insect voices already; last time the chorus took till morning.
Brecca sits against the hall wall, silent since the pulse, studying her open hands.
Wren does not ask her what she feels.
'One hundred and twelve breaths. I will remember.' 'Write it down.' 'I do not write. I carry.'
The fire burns down as the chorus adds a fourth voice, then a fifth.
Wren journals: the gap retreated a degree, 112 breaths, five people held.
The count restarts at zero, and now it feels like counting toward something.
